details: CONFIRMED by a scan of the branch's queue files. The brief: "rewrites the 24 open items that hold such entries ... commit with the
change"; the item's what and Done list it. Without it the start filter still holds the 13 items held by folders, which is the stated
why of the move, and every later where edit of those items is now refused (see F2). The count is 26 now (items added since the plan).
Size: 30 minutes (26 edits, each choosing the files).
evidence: python3 scan over .relay/queue/*.json (open, path endswith / or isdir or *?[) -> 26
failing_case: At HEAD 1ac071a1, the open items under .relay/queue/ of the branch: 26 hold a `where` entry that is a folder or a pattern
No commit of the branch touches .relay/queue. The item's Done says "the 24 items are rewritten" and asks to record which items the
start filter holds before and after; neither was done. Expected: 0 open items with such an entry, each fixed by one
`relay queue edit` with because "folder entry named as a file", and the before/after held count recorded.
fix_hint: From this worktree's bin/relay, one `relay queue edit <slug> where '<all folder lines>' '<files>' --because "folder entry named as a file"`
per item (old may span several lines, so one call fixes all entries of an item), then commit; record the start filter's held items before and after.
pass_cases: 1. Every open item: no where entry whose path ends in "/", names an existing directory, or holds * ? [ -> 0 such items (the scan below prints 0).
2. a-gate-log-keeps-failure-lines-of-any-length: the pattern ".relay/checks/*.gate.log" becomes the files it names (or the file the fix will change), not a glob.
3. Each rewritten item carries one fact note "Edited where: folder entry named as a file" (one relay queue edit per item).
4. Items with only file entries (e.g. refuse-folder-and-pattern-entries-in-where itself) are unchanged.
5. The start filter's held count before and after is recorded in the item or the hand-back (13 of 29 held by folders before).
reason: where_folders over head's open items: 0 flagged.

details: CONFIRMED by a scratch test subclassing WhereFiles: the refusal above is printed. edit() runs where_folders(after, repo) over the whole
new list, including entries carried over from `before`. Principle 10 (a refusal names the next step): here the next step it names was
evidence: REFUSED: nothing edited: where element 2 `docs/` is a folder: name the file you will change (a new file is fine, e.g. lib/relay_cmd/digest.py)
failing_case: Item with where ["lib/ (modules)", "docs/ (notes)"]. `relay queue edit <slug> where "lib/ (modules)" "lib/relay_cmd/digest.py" --because ...`
-> Refused "nothing edited: where element 2 `docs/` is a folder: name the file you will change". The person did name a file; the
refusal points at an entry they did not touch and does not say that every folder entry must be fixed in the same edit. On the 26
stored items (F1), 4 have two or more folder entries, and any where edit of them (adding a file, fixing one entry) is refused.
Expected: either the edit is accepted (only entries new in `after` are judged), or the refusal says to replace all folder entries in one edit.
fix_hint: In edit, judge only the entries of `after` not in `before`: where_folders([x for x in after if x not in before], ...) with the element
numbers taken from `after`; or keep the whole-list check and add to the text "(already stored: replace every folder entry in one edit; old may span lines)". Add the case to tests/test_queue_where.py.
pass_cases: 1. where ["lib/ (modules)", "docs/ (notes)"], edit "lib/ (modules)" -> "lib/relay_cmd/digest.py": accepted with where ["lib/relay_cmd/digest.py", "docs/ (notes)"], or refused with a text that names element 2 as already stored and says to replace it in the same edit.
2. where ["lib/relay_other.py"], edit to "lib/": refused "nothing edited: where element 1 `lib/` is a folder" (today's test_edit_gives_the_same_verdicts).
4. where ["lib/ (a)", "docs/ (b)"], one edit whose old covers both lines, new two files: accepted.
findings.summary: edit of one where entry is refused for another, untouched folder entry of the same item
